overview.description: Briscola is Italy's most beloved card game, a point-trick game played with the distinctive 40-card Italian deck (suits: coins, cups, batons, swords). Each player holds 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is revealed by the last card dealt, which stays visible until taken. The unusual ranking system (Ace > 3 > King > Queen > Jack > 7-2 in point order) makes Briscola distinct from virtually every other card game in the world.
overview.deck: 40 cards (Italian deck; or French 52-card deck stripped to 40)

history.origins: Briscola developed in Italy from older European Ace-Ten card games. The word 'briscola' means trump in Italian. The game is one of the founding pillars of Mediterranean card culture.
timeline: 1800s: Standard rules codified across Italian regions.
Present: National game of Italy; second only to Scopa in popularity. Also played across the Mediterranean (Croatia/Slovenia as Briškula, Portugal as Bisca, Spain as Brisca).
history.evolution: Briscola Chiamata (5-player 'called' Briscola) is widely considered the most sophisticated variant. Each of the sibling games (Bisca, Brisca) has distinct quirks: Bisca uses the 7 instead of the 3 as the second trump.
history.cultural: Briscola is deeply embedded in Italian daily life, played in courts, piazzas, cafes, and family homes. The 5-player Chiamata version is the prestige variant.

setup.deck: 40 cards. Italian deck: A, 3, Re (K), Cavallo (Q), Fante (J), 7, 6, 5, 4, 2 in 4 suits. OR: French deck stripped of 8s, 9s, 10s.
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards to each player, then turn one card face-up beside the remaining stockâ€”that card's suit is Briscola (trump). Stock placed crosswise on trump card, leaving suit visible.

rules.objective: Score 61 or more of the 120 available card points.
rules.gameplay: Each trick: non-dealer leads any card. No follow-suit obligation. Opponent plays any card. Trick won by higher Briscola (trump) played, OR higher of led suit if no Briscola. Winner draws first from stock; loser draws second. Winner leads next. Final trick: trump indicator card is last taken from stock.
keyRules: Trump (Briscola) beats all off-suit cards regardless of rank.
The trump-indicator card is taken by the winner of the last draw-phase trick.
Pointing cards: only A, 3, K, Q, J have value.

strategy.basic: Lead worthless cards (7-2) to bait opponents into spending Aces or 3s on nothing-tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Economy: Don't trump low-value tricks. Save your Briscola Ace for the opponent's Ace-led trick.
strategy.advanced: End-of-Stock Timing: Once the stock depletes, you know both hands. Calculate exactly who has which trump card. A Briscola 3 in hand is a second-place trumpâ€”use it to steal the opponent's 7 so they can't counter your Briscola Ace.
tips: The 3 of Briscola (trump) is worth 10 pointsâ€”nearly as valuable as the Ace. Protect it.
Leading a Briscola early can be riskyâ€”you might force the opponent to play a higher trump you can't beat.

list.name: Briscola Chiamata (Called Briscola)
list.description: 5-player variant. Each player bids to name trump AND secretly call an ally by naming a specific card. The called card owner becomes partner without revealing themselves.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Five-player called Briscola changes bidding and partnerships; engine overrides for those structures are not yet modeled.

list.name: Briscola Scoperta (Open Briscola)
list.description: Some or all cards played face-up. Reduces luck, increases skill.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Open Briscola exposes hands and stock face up; these information changes are described in text but not encoded as engine overrides yet.

difficulty.easy: Leads worst cards. Plays trump freely.
difficulty.medium: Counts trump played. Saves Ace for high-value tricks. Avoids gifting Aces.
difficulty.hard: Full card tracker. Calculates exact EV of each play. Manages trump economy perfectly. Adjusts based on whether opponent has drawn trump indicator card.

considerations: No-follow-suit makes hand reading much harder.
The unusual ranking (A > 3 > K...) needs to be encoded explicitly.
Stock depletion is a major information state change.

additional: Italian Card Games (Paolo Marino, Paolo Ronzoni)

ante.reason: Briscola is a trick-taking game; object is to take cards for points. No betting.

deal.reason: Briscola uses custom deal phase (deal_3_each_turn_trump); standard deal action not used.

reveal_market.reason: One card turned face-up for trump; no market. Stock placed beside trump card.

buy_market.reason: No market or buying; players deal and draw from stock only.

buy_stock.reason: Players draw from stock after each trick; no purchase mechanic.

fold.reason: Trick-taking; no betting or fold. Each trick both players play a card.

bet.reason: No betting; score by card points won in tricks.

declare.reason: Game ends when all cards played; points counted from won tricks. No declaration.

reveal_hand.reason: No showdown; count points from tricks won at end.

award_pot.reason: No pot; winner is higher point total from tricks.

play_card.description: Play a legal card according to current phase rules.
play_card.constraints: Legal during play phases when the selected card satisfies phase/trick constraints.

draw.reason: Winner and loser draw after each trick; modeled in trick phase, not standalone.

discard.reason: Play card to trick; winner takes both. No discard-from-hand.

pass.reason: No pass; second player may play any card (no follow-suit).

bid.reason: Basic Briscola has no bidding. Briscola Chiamata (5p) adds it.

meld.reason: Trick-taking; no melding. Score from cards won in tricks.

go_out.reason: Game ends when all cards played; no go-out mechanic.

notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Play cards to trick; winner takes both. No discard pile.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trump beats any non-trump; when same suit led, higher rank wins; when trump is played, highest trump wins.

edgeCases.text: When stock is exhausted, next player to draw takes the face-up trump card; play continues without drawing until all cards played.
Some play: if turned card is Ace or Three, put it back and turn another for trump.

customActions.description: Deal 3 cards to each player and turn one card for trump.
Play any card to the trick (no follow-suit obligation).

engine.handRankingSystem: Not a poker-hand game; tricks score via Briscola card-point values.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 40-card Italian deck: four suits (swords, batons, cups, coins) with ten ranks each (ace, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and three face cards). No jokers; used for Briscola where the turned card sets trump.
engine.suitDescription: Four Italian suits (swords, batons, cups, coins). Trump is the suit of the card turned after the deal; it outranks the other three suits. Follow suit when able; each suit has ten cards.
engine.rankDescription: Ten ranks per suit in Italian order (ace, two, three, four, five, six, seven, then face cards). Point values: ace 11, three 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2; others zero. Trick order follows Briscola rules.

hero.title: BRISCOLA
hero.subtitle: Italia Gioca
hero.tagline: The Ace is power. The Three is glory. Guard both.

synthesis.shortDescription: Italy's national card game and the template for Bisca and Brisca. A deceptively simple point-trick game where no-suit-obligation creates beautiful chaos, and the Ace and Three of trumps are worth nearly half the points in the game.

prompts.human: Your opponent leads a mid-card Coin. You hold the Ace of Cups (Briscola, 11 pts) and the 3 of Coins (a 10-pt non-trump). Don't waste your Briscola Ace on this trickâ€”play the 3 of Coins. If they can't beat it, you win 0 pts on the trick but save your Ace for a bigger moment.
prompts.ai: Game: Briscola. Italian 40-card. Ranking: A(11)>3(10)>K(4)>Q(3)>J(2)>others(0). No follow-suit. Trump=Briscola. Target: 61 points.

scoring.winCondition: First to 61 card points wins the deal.
